========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Withdrawn? No, I wouldn't say that. I still see my clients every week, and I talk to my sister on the phone, even if she does drive me up the wall with her catalog vitamins. I haven't lost interest in my shows or anything. 

Speaking of my shows, they moved the time slot for Wheel of Fortune in my area, and it completely threw off my whole evening routine. It used to be right after the local news, perfectly timed for when I sit down with my dinner, but now they've swapped it with some syndicated sitcom from the nineties. I don't know who makes these decisions at the network, but they clearly don't think about the people who actually watch television. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins—she's the one with the terrible rhododendrons that always drop leaves in my driveway—she actually called the station to complain. Can you imagine? Waiting on hold for twenty minutes just to yell at some poor intern about a game show. 

Though I will say, those rhododendrons are a menace. I spend half my Saturday morning just sweeping the driveway because if it rains, those leaves turn to absolute mush, and they stain the concrete. I bought this heavy-duty push broom from the hardware store, the one with the stiff bristles, but the handle is just a fraction too short. It makes my lower back ache if I use it for more than ten minutes. I should probably just get a leaf blower, but the gas ones are so loud and they smell terrible, and the battery ones never hold a charge long enough to finish the job. 

But no, I'm still doing all the things I usually do. Not withdrawn at all.

They don't take a break just because I'm tired.\n\nDoctor: How long have you been hearing the woman’s voice and believing that people are watching you like this?\n\nPatient: Well, let me think... it's been about 11 months now that the voice and the feeling of them watching us has been going on. I know it's been 11 months because it started right around the time I had to buy a new vacuum cleaner for my housekeeping jobs. The motor on my old one just completely burned out right in the middle of a shift. It smelled like burning rubber all over Mrs. Gable's living room! I was so embarrassed. I had to run right out to the big store on the highway and buy a new one that same afternoon. I ended up getting this purple one with a special attachment for pet hair, which is honestly an absolute lifesaver because Mrs. Gable has two of those fluffy white cats. Persian cats, I think they're called? They shed everywhere. You just look at them and fur floats into the air. I spend half my morning just trying to get the hair off her dark blue velvet sofa. Who buys a velvet sofa when they have cats, anyway? It just doesn't make any sense to me. People really don't think ahead when they decorate. Like my sister, she bought a pure white rug for her front entryway, and with all the mud we get in the spring, it was ruined in a week. But anyway, yes, it's been about 11 months since the voice and the watching started.\n\nDoctor: During the past 11 months, have you had a period of at least two weeks when you were depressed or very high in mood, and the voice and watching were present only during that time?\n\nPatient: Well, I don't know about *only* during that time, but I definitely had them when my mood was just... up in the clouds, I guess you'd say. There were a few weeks where I barely slept a wink, maybe two hours a night, and I was just running everywhere. I'd go from cleaning three houses in a row straight over to the church to organize the pantry, and the whole time, that woman's voice was right there with me, and I just *knew* they were tracking the routes I was taking around town. Speaking of the church pantry, you wouldn't believe the things people donate. Last month, someone dropped off six cans of cranberry sauce that expired in 2018! I mean, who keeps cranberry sauce that long? And they just toss it in the donation bin like they're doing some grand favor. I had to throw the whole lot out. Father Thomas hates wasting food, but I told him, \"Father, we can't be giving people botulism for the holidays.\" He agreed, of course. He's such a sweet man, but he really doesn't know the first thing about organizing a kitchen. He keeps the flour right next to the sink! It's a disaster waiting to happen. But yes, during those weeks when I had all that energy and no sleep, the voice and the tracking were definitely happening right along with it.\n\nDoctor: Have there also been times over the past 11 months when the voice and the feeling that people were watching you were present even though you were not depressed, very high, or not sleeping much?\n\nPatient: Well, yes, actually, I think I mentioned it earlier. There was that quieter spell, you know? It lasted for several weeks where I wasn't running around like a chicken with its head cut off, and I was actually sleeping a lot more. I wasn't rushing from house to house cleaning nearly as much. But even during that quieter time, when I felt so drained, I still heard that woman's voice by the kitchen window, and I still knew the agency was out there watching us. They never stop. It's like my neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he never stops mowing his lawn. I swear, he's out there three times a week with that loud gas mower. And he always does it right when I'm trying to watch my afternoon shows. It's just so inconsiderate. I don't understand why people can't just use a push mower, or at least wait until the evening. His grass isn't even that long! He just likes the noise, I think. He also leaves his garbage cans out by the curb for three days after pickup. It drives the neighborhood association crazy. They send him letters, but he just ignores them. Anyway, yes, even when I wasn't full of energy or depressed, the voice and the watching were still there.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any other unusual experiences, like feeling that your thoughts are being broadcast, controlled, or inserted by someone else?\n\nPatient: Well, no... I don't think so. My thoughts are just my own. I mean, nobody is putting them in my head or broadcasting them on the radio or anything like that. Mostly I'm just thinking about my schedule, or what I need to pick up at the store for my next shift. \n\nLike just yesterday, I was thinking about how I need to get more of that lemon wood polish. The store brand, not the name brand. Though, honestly, they changed the formula on the name brand recently, which is why I switched. The bottle looks exactly the same, but the plastic cap is a slightly lighter yellow now, and I swear to you, it leaves this awful cloudy streak on mahogany. I used it on Mrs. Gable's dining table last week and it took me an extra twenty minutes just to buff it out with a microfiber cloth. And time is money in my line of work! You just don't see men dressing like that anymore, do you? Everyone is so casual nowadays, wearing sweatpants to the grocery store like they just rolled right out of bed. It's a shame, people used to take pride in how they presented themselves in public. My mother would have never let us out of the house in sweatpants. \n\nBut anyway, what were you asking? Oh, about my thoughts. No, nothing unusual like that, just my regular thinking.\n\nDoctor: Over the past 11 months, have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day?\n\nPatient: Depressed? You have to, right? If you stop, the dust just settles. \n\nAnd speaking of dust, you wouldn't believe the amount of dust that accumulates on ceiling fan blades. It's like people just forget they exist up there! I was at the Miller house on Tuesday, and I don't think they've dusted their bedroom fan since the Bush administration. I tried it once on these beautiful French doors at the Peterson house, and my fingers were pitch black by the time I finished the living room. I had to scrub them with Dawn dish soap for ten minutes, and that just ruins your cuticles. It makes my lower back ache if I use it for more than ten minutes.
